A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mechanism-design and bandit research despite the changed title. Their main texts, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–B are available and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original bandit and simulated auction experiments in Section 7 and Appendix A.4, including sample requirements, utility and revenue errors, and computational resource measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments in Section 8 and Appendix A.4, with results in Figures 1–9 and Table 1.

M1.justification: V1's Algorithms 2–3 reuse samples collected while identifying an arm and supplement them only when necessary. V2's Algorithm 2 instead draws a fixed batch of fresh samples after arm identification. This changes the general BME procedure; the analytical mechanism and experimentally used SE-BME remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Bernoulli bandits with equally spaced means and the same synthetic double-sided auction environment. The player/type ranges and represented tasks are retained; no new dataset or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: Figure 3 still compares SE-BME with SE-BAI, and the mechanism experiments retain exact computation as their comparator. The BAI comparison remains in Appendix A.4.1 despite losing its main-text summary.

E3.justification: The SBB headings in Figures 2, 7, and 8 change from v1's equations (57)–(58) to v2's rho=0 and equations (12)–(13), (24), invoking an alternative theta prescription. This changes the reported construction, but Appendix A.4.3 still states the original theta=0 settings and corresponding formulas. The description is therefore inconsistent, without establishing that experiments changed. Other evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: The same analyses remain: sample trajectories, scaling with players and types, utility and revenue sensitivity to estimation, the rho'=0.1 adjustment, and RMSE versus sampling accuracy. Appendix relocation and rewritten summaries do not add or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten repetitions for the bandit comparison, its plotted standard deviations, and ten random seeds for utility/revenue and RMSE experiments. Table 1 retains the same seed-aggregation notes. Experimental uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–9 retain identical plotted data, and Table 1 retains all runtime and memory values. The reported scaling, SE-BME/SE-BAI comparisons, utility/revenue discrepancies, and RMSE trends are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 revises Lemma 4's proof to match fresh sampling: v1 applies Hoeffding's inequality conditional on an adaptively selected arm and sample count, whereas v2 uses a fixed batch collected after selection. This repairs a substantive local proof issue while preserving the PAC bound and asymptotic rate. Other theoretical statements are largely merged, reordered, or renumbered.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain analytical optimal LP solutions, feasibility characterization under independent types, asymptotically optimal PAC best-mean estimation, and empirical scaling to 128 players. The new title and reordered contribution narrative do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations for sample savings and greater revenue sensitivity, together with limitations concerning dependent types, guarantees only in expectation, finite experimental scale, continuous types, and fairness. The rewritten discussion adds no substantive new interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: The data-generation instructions, greedy allocation procedure, caching explanation, single-core cloud execution, memory requirements, and resource table are retained. Both describe code as supplementary material with public release planned upon acceptance.

R1.justification: V2 removes the citations to Conitzer and Sandholm (2002) and Sandholm (2003). It also explicitly clarifies that the prior trading-network framework permits any finite player count, while its reported numerical application involved two players. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial main-text passages are extensively rewritten. V1's Section 6 becomes separate sections on mechanism PAC guarantees and BME complexity, with the guarantees presented first. Lemmas and corollaries are consolidated, and the title, affiliation information, and acknowledgements change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different conference-style layout, replacing the separate title page with an integrated title, author block, abstract, and introduction. Typography, text width, figure sizing and placement, and algorithm placement change throughout. All nine figures and the table remain, with revised panel headings and captions.

improvement.justification: The fresh-sample estimator and revised Lemma 4 proof repair the dependence problem in v1's concentration argument, strengthening support for the existing PAC upper bound. Reorganizing the mechanism guarantees before the bandit complexity analysis also improves clarity. These gains outweigh the loss of sample reuse, although inconsistent SBB panel references remain a documentation drawback.
